sam_dev: Heads-up — mypy is blowing up in the sample app after the latest autogen run. Repro below, short thread.
ana: ugh, can you paste the error and the generated model snippet?
sam_dev: sure. repro steps: checkout main, pip install -r requirements.txt, regenerate models with `python -m tools.autogen models`, then run `mypy sampleapp --strict`.
mypy output (trimmed):
```
sampleapp/handlers.py:47: error: Incompatible types in assignment (expression has type "List[Dict[str, Any]]", variable has type "Dict[str, Any]")  [assignment]
sampleapp/handlers.py:75: error: Argument 1 to "process_prompt" has incompatible type "None"; expected "str"  [arg-type]
Found 2 errors in 1 file (checked 12 source files)
```
sam_dev: generated model (from `models.py`):
```
class Prompt(BaseModel):
    id: str
    metadata: dict[str, Any]
    extra: Optional[str] = None
```
sam_dev: but the runtime payload for metadata sometimes comes back as a list (legacy clients send array), and our handlers do `if 'tags' in p.metadata:` which assumes mapping. mypy flagged the assignment earlier because the model is `dict[...]` but we assign from parsed json which is typed as `List[Dict[str, Any]]` in some code paths.
mike_infra: I think the generator template is too opinionated: it picks `dict[str, Any]` whenever shape is unknown, but if example samples include both dict and list it should use `Any` or `Union[dict[str, Any], list[Any]]` (or `object` and runtime guards). Right now it doesn't preserve union types from the samples.
mike_infra: minimal fix: change autogen to emit `metadata: Any` when inconsistent shapes are detected, or better: emit `Union[dict[str, Any], list[Any]]` when both observed. Also make it prefer `Optional[...]` for missing fields even if default not provided.
taylor: fwiw this also breaks mypy strict mode because the generator omits `Optional` for fields that are sometimes null in examples. We should run a quick heuristic: if any example value is `null` -> use `Optional[...]`.
jessica: I can take the PR. Two additional asks:
- add a small test that runs `mypy` on the generated sampleapp to catch regressions
- update the autogen docs that explain why sometimes we use `Any` vs `dict` vs `Union`
sam_dev: thanks. Another subtle thing: async client stubs use `str` for streaming events but our ws layer yields `bytes` in some envs, so generated handler signatures don't match the runtime type. We should unify client transport to always decode to text or change stubs to `Union[str, bytes]`.
ana: good catch. that explains a flake I saw in dev infra where stream tests fail only on python3.11 worker.
mike_infra: plan: I'll put up a draft PR to change autogen heuristics -> prefer `Union[...]` when multiple concrete types appear, fallback to `Any` when >2 shapes, and mark fields `Optional` if any sample is null. Also add a lint step that runs a small mypy check on the sample app.
jessica: awesome, I'll pair-review. tagging @ci-bot to run the current failing matrix job.
ci-bot: CI job `sampleapp-mypy` failed on commit abc123 — logs uploaded: https://ci.internal.redwood/sampleapp-mypy/abc123 :eyes:
sam_dev: cool. thanks all. leaving this thread for the PR. :thumbsup:
